description: Experience the velvety richness of authentic Indian Butter Chicken, a cherished dish where tender chicken is simmered in a creamy tomato-based sauce. This Murgh Makhani recipe promises a symphony of mild spices and buttery goodness, perfect for a comforting and satisfying meal. Its vibrant flavors and smooth texture make it a beloved classic across the globe.

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a bowl, combine chicken pieces with yogurt, 1/2 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, chili powder, turmeric, 1/2 tsp garam masala, and a pinch of salt. Mix well and let it marinate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours in the refrigerator.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tbsp butter in a large pan or Dutch oven over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken and cook in batches until browned and lightly cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per batch. Remove chicken from the pan and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Sauce Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add another 1 tbsp butter. Once melted, add the chopped onion and saute until translucent and softened, about 5-7 minutes. Add the remaining 1/2 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant.

instructions.title: Simmer the Tomato Sauce
instructions.text: Stir in the crushed tomatoes, soaked cashews, and 1/2 cup water. Bring the mixture to a simmer, then reduce heat to low, cover, and cook for 10-15 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld. Remove from heat and let it cool slightly.

instructions.title: Blend the Sauce
instructions.text: Carefully transfer the cooled tomato mixture to a blender. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. For an extra smooth sauce, pass it through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan. This step is crucial for the authentic silky texture.

instructions.title: Finish the Butter Chicken
instructions.text: Return the pan with the blended sauce to medium-low heat. Add the cooked chicken, remaining 2 tbsp butter, heavy cream, 1/2 tsp garam masala, crushed fenugreek leaves (if using), and sugar. Stir gently and simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors and heat through. Adjust salt and sugar to your preference.

tips: For best results, marinate the chicken overnight to allow the flavors to deeply penetrate the meat, resulting in more tender and flavorful chicken.
Using good quality canned crushed tomatoes makes a big difference in the sauce's flavor. Also, dont skip the cashews; they add richness and thickness.
Serve Butter Chicken piping hot with freshly made naan bread, steamed basmati rice, or jeera rice to soak up all the delicious gravy.
article:
Butter Chicken, known in India as Murgh Makhani, is one of the world's most beloved and iconic Indian dishes. Its rich, creamy, and subtly spiced tomato-based sauce, enveloping tender pieces of marinated chicken, has captured the hearts and palates of food enthusiasts everywhere. Perfect as a comforting Indian lunch recipe or a special dinner, this dish offers a symphony of flavors that is both luxurious and deeply satisfying. If you've ever dreamt of recreating that restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home, you're in the right place. This comprehensive guide will walk you through everything you need to know to master this culinary masterpiece.

## What is Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani?

Murgh Makhani, literally translating to "chicken with butter," originated in the 1950s at the Moti Mahal restaurant in Delhi, India. It was purportedly created by accident, using leftover tandoori chicken simmered in a rich tomato gravy enriched with butter and cream. The result was a revelation: a mild yet intensely flavorful curry that balances tanginess from tomatoes, sweetness from honey or sugar, and a profound richness from butter and cream. Unlike many spicier Indian curries, Butter Chicken is known for its smooth, velvety texture and balanced flavor profile, making it universally appealing. It's truly a testament to Indian culinary ingenuity and a staple in Indian lunch recipes worldwide.

## Ingredients You Need

To create authentic Butter Chicken, you'll need a combination of fresh ingredients and aromatic spices.

**For the Chicken Marinade:**
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breast, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri for color, or regular for heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice

**For the Makhani Sauce:**
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter
*   1 tablespoon oil (vegetable or canola)
*   1 large onion, finely chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon salt (or to taste)
*   1 can (400g) crushed tomatoes or 3-4 medium tomatoes, pureed
*   1/4 cup raw cashews (soaked in warm water for 15 minutes, optional)
*   1/2 cup water (for blending)
*   1/2 cup heavy cream
*   1 tablespoon honey or sugar (adjust to taste)
*   1 teaspoon kasuri methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped (for garnish)

## Step-by-Step Instructions

Creating Murgh Makhani is a process of layering flavors. Follow these steps for a delicious outcome:

**1. Marinate the Chicken:** In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all marinade ingredients. Mix well to ensure the chicken is evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or ideally 2-4 hours, or even overnight for maximum flavor.

**2. Cook the Chicken:** You have a few options here.
    *   **Pan-fry:** Heat a little oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken in batches (don't overcrowd the pan) and cook until browned and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side. Set aside.
    *   **Grill/Bake:** For a more authentic smoky flavor, you can grill the chicken or bake it in a preheated oven at 200°C (400°F) for 15-20 minutes until cooked.

**3. Prepare the Sauce Base:** In a large pot or Dutch oven, melt butter and oil over medium heat. Add the chopped onions and sauté until translucent and lightly golden, about 8-10 minutes. Add the ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant. Stir in the red chili powder, turmeric powder, and garam masala. Cook for 30 seconds, stirring constantly to prevent burning.

**4. Simmer and Blend the Sauce:** Pour in the crushed tomatoes (or pureed fresh tomatoes), salt, and soaked cashews (if using). Bring to a simmer, then reduce heat, cover, and cook for 15-20 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes have broken down and the sauce has thickened slightly. Remove from heat and let it cool for a few minutes. Carefully transfer the sauce mixture to a blender (or use an immersion blender) and blend until completely smooth. For an extra silky sauce, pass it through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pot.

**5. Finish the Murgh Makhani:** Return the smooth sauce to the pot over medium-low heat. Stir in the heavy cream and honey (or sugar). Add the cooked chicken pieces and the crushed kasuri methi. Simmer for another 5-10 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the rich sauce. Taste and adjust seasoning, adding more salt, honey, or a pinch of chili powder if needed.

**6. Garnish and Serve:** Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro and a swirl of extra cream, if desired.

## Pro Tips for the Best Results

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will become, contributing significantly to the final Butter Chicken taste.
*   **Blend Until Silky Smooth:** A hallmark of great Murgh Makhani is its incredibly smooth sauce. Invest time in blending the sauce thoroughly. Straining it through a fine-mesh sieve after blending is a step many restaurants take and makes a noticeable difference in texture.
*   **Don't Fear the Fat:** Butter and cream are fundamental to Butter Chicken. While you can opt for low-fat alternatives, the authentic richness comes from using full-fat ingredients.
*   **Toast Kasuri Methi:** Before adding kasuri methi, gently rub it between your palms or lightly toast it in a dry pan for a few seconds. This releases its aromatic oils and enhances its distinctive flavor.
*   **Balance Sweetness and Tang:** The perfect Butter Chicken strikes a balance between the tang of tomatoes and the sweetness of honey or sugar. Adjust these to your personal preference. A little bit of fresh lemon juice at the end can also brighten the flavors.
*   **The Smoky Touch (Dhungaar):** For an authentic smoky flavor, heat a small piece of charcoal until glowing red. Place it in a small bowl inside your pot of finished Murgh Makhani, drizzle a teaspoon of ghee or oil over the charcoal, and quickly cover the pot for 2-3 minutes. This traditional Indian smoking technique imparts a wonderful aroma.

## Serving Suggestions

Butter Chicken Murgh Makhani is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments.
*   **Indian Breads:** The classic pairing is with warm, fluffy naan bread, roti, or laccha paratha, perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich sauce.
*   **Rice:** Basmati rice, plain or jeera rice (cumin-flavored rice), is another excellent choice, providing a neutral base to soak up the luxurious curry.
*   **Side Salads:** A simple kachumber salad (diced cucumber, tomato, onion with lemon juice) offers a refreshing contrast.
*   **Yogurt:** A side of plain yogurt or raita (yogurt with cucumber and mint) can help balance the richness.
*   **Complete Meal:** Serve it alongside other Indian dishes like dal, saag paneer, or vegetable curries for a grand feast.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken is a delight, you can easily adapt this recipe to suit different dietary needs or preferences.
*   **Vegetarian Murgh Makhani:** Replace the chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese) for Paneer Makhani, or use firm tofu, chickpeas, or a medley of vegetables like cauliflower, potatoes, and peas.
*   **Healthier Options:** To reduce calories, use less butter and cream, opting for low-fat cream or even coconut milk for a slightly different flavor profile. You can also increase the vegetable content in the sauce.
*   **Nut-Free:** If you have a nut allergy, you can substitute cashews with sunflower seeds (soaked) or simply omit them and rely on a bit more cream or tomato paste for thickness.
*   **Spice Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder to your liking. For a milder curry, use Kashmiri chili powder which provides color without much heat. For more kick, add a pinch of cayenne pepper.
*   **Smoky Flavor without Charcoal:** A tiny drop of liquid smoke can be added to the sauce, but use sparingly as it can be overpowering.

Bringing the taste of authentic Butter Chicken into your home is an incredibly rewarding experience. With this recipe, you can create a dish that rivals any restaurant, offering a rich, comforting, and unforgettable Indian lunch recipe that your family and friends will adore. Enjoy the journey of making this culinary gem!
